title: Allah's Mercy and Human Despair
summary: This Hadith discusses Allah's boundless mercy, which He divided into 100 parts. One part is shared among all creatures in the world, fostering love and kindness. The remaining 99 parts are reserved for the believers in the Hereafter, promising immense blessings. Believers are urged not to despair of Allah's mercy, as despairing is viewed as a sign of disbelief.
translation:
In the Holy Quran, it is stated, 'Do not despair of the mercy of Allah.' Despair is a sign of disbelief because Allah is most merciful. The Hadith explains further: Allah created mercy in 100 parts, sending one part to the world, encompassing humans, jinn, animals, and all creatures. All mutual affection and kindness in the world stem from just this one part of mercy. The love a person has for family, the bond between teachers and students, and admiration for doers of good all draw from this single part. The love in people's hearts for the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and Allah originates from this same mercy.

This one portion of mercy encompasses the entire universe, yet seems insufficient compared to the remaining 99 parts kept by Allah for the Day of Judgment, to be showered upon believers and the righteous, those who believe in Allah and the Last Day. Thus, they will benefit greatly, be saved from hellfire, granted entry into paradise, and blessed with Allah’s vision. Therefore, one must never despair of Allah’s mercy, regardless of their sins.

Even if a person tires from sinning, Allah never tires of forgiving because weariness is a flaw, and Allah is free from defects. Hence, never despair, no matter the sins—repent in solitude, weep to Allah. When closeness to Allah is achieved, worldly difficulties appear trivial, making worship easier, leading to happiness in this life and the next. Relatives, parents, children, spouses, and colleagues will all be pleased as duties are fulfilled.

Those who despair of Allah’s mercy feel overwhelmed, thinking they must manage everything themselves. This leads to constant misfortune and stress, sometimes even self-destruction. Thus, one should never despair of Allah’s mercy. Only non-believers lose hope in it. Reminded of Allah’s greatness, a believer cannot despair. We should pray, repent earnestly, and lighten our sin burdens, asking Allah to accept our repentance and grant us abundant mercy.
